summary: FlameIntel is an AI-powered web dashboard designed to make NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion research easier to explore, understand, and use. The platform helps researchers identify investigations relevant to fire safety in spacecraft, the International Space Station, lunar and Mars habitats, and pressurized rovers. Through an Investigation Explorer, AI Research Assistant, and Data Explorer, users can search scientific studies, obtain evidence-based summaries, inspect available experimental datasets, and assess their suitability for predictive modeling. FlameIntel also connects research findings to potential improvements in fire suppression, smoke detection, fire-resistant materials, and crew protection, while highlighting possible applications on Earth. By organizing complex scientific information into an accessible and interactive platform, FlameIntel supports research discovery, data-driven analysis, and the development of safer environments for future human space exploration.
details:
Project Details

FlameIntel is an AI-powered web dashboard designed to transform NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion research into accessible and useful fire-safety intelligence. The platform helps users explore scientific investigations related to fire behavior in spacecraft, the International Space Station (ISS), lunar and Mars habitats, and pressurized rovers.

The project works through several interconnected components. The Investigation Explorer allows users to search, filter, and rank investigations according to their research topics, experimental conditions, and relevance to a selected space environment. The AI Research Assistant uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer questions about indexed scientific documents, provide summaries, and link responses to their sources. The Data Explorer helps users inspect available experimental datasets, understand their variables and units, identify missing data, and evaluate their potential suitability for predictive modeling. Additionally, Fire Safety Insights connects research findings to potential improvements in fire suppression, smoke detection, fire-resistant materials, and crew protection.

The main benefit of FlameIntel is reducing the difficulty of discovering and understanding complex scientific information. Instead of manually searching through numerous records and publications, researchers can access relevant information through a unified, interactive platform. Its intended impact is to support data-driven fire-safety research and contribute to the development of safer environments for future human space exploration, while also exploring potential applications on Earth.

The proposed technical approach includes Next.js, React, and TypeScript for the frontend; Python and FastAPI for the backend; PostgreSQL for structured data storage; Pandas for data processing; and AI models with RAG for intelligent search and research assistance. The project is creative because it combines scientific data exploration, explainable AI-based relevance ranking, document-grounded question answering, and fire-safety insight discovery in one platform. Our team considers scientific reliability, data availability, source traceability, experimental limitations, and the differences between space environments to ensure that generated insights remain evidence-based and transparent.
